subject: Biotechnology
title: De-Extinction Ethics
description: A quick, practical guide to De-Extinction Ethics.

hook.text: Bring back the woolly mammoth — Colossal Biosciences says it can. But should we resurrect extinct species?

buildup.text: Ancient DNA from frozen specimens provides the blueprint — CRISPR edits cold-adapted genes into Asian elephant cells.

discovery.text: Proponents argue de-extinction restores ecosystem functions — mammoths could revive grasslands and slow Arctic permafrost thawing.

twist.text: Critics say de-extinction diverts funds from conserving living species — why resurrect the dead when the living need help?

climax.text: A resurrected mammoth is not a real mammoth — it is an elephant-mammoth hybrid with no mammoth culture or social knowledge.

punchline.text: Can we bring them back? Probably. Should we? That is the harder question.

quiz.question: Why would a de-extincted mammoth not truly be a woolly mammoth?
options: It would be too small to survive in cold climates
It would be a genetically engineered elephant-mammoth hybrid lacking the social behaviors and culture of real mammoths
Ancient mammoth DNA has degraded too much to provide any useful genetic information
